user.title: Powerwall TEDAPI
user.description: Find the Powerwall on your network. Signed (v1r) access gives local readings, local control and battery dispatch; this wizard can register the key it needs.

gateway.title: Gateway
gateway.description:
**Gateway address:** the Powerwall's address on your home network (the router lists it as `teslapw_…`; reserving the address helps, but Home Assistant also follows the gateway when the router reports a new address). Use `192.168.91.1` only if Home Assistant is on the Powerwall's own Wi-Fi network.

**Gateway password:** printed on the QR sticker inside the Powerwall's cover (Powerwall 3: behind the front glass, lower left). Home Assistant uses its last 5 characters to log in to the gateway; it is checked now.

data_description.host: The gateway's address on your home network, for example `192.168.1.50`. Your router lists it as `teslapw_…`.
data_description.gw_pwd: The last 5 characters of the password on the QR sticker inside the Powerwall's cover (Powerwall 3: behind the front glass, lower left), or the whole password. Letters are upper case.
data_description.wifi_host: The Powerwall's Wi-Fi hotspot, used over the same signed connection when the home-network address stops answering. Leave empty if Home Assistant cannot reach the hotspot.

access.title: Choose how to connect
access.description: Signed (v1r) access needs a key that this Powerwall trusts.

menu_options.key_upload: Upload a key that is already registered

key_upload.title: Upload the key
key_upload.description: Upload the PEM private key of a key registered with this Powerwall (for example with `python -m pypowerwall register`, state VERIFIED). It is copied into the `tesla_tedapi` folder of your configuration and readable only by Home Assistant.

data.cloud_backup: Link a Tesla account as a backup for settings

data_description.key_file: The private key file (`.pem`, starts with `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` or `-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----`) whose public key is registered and VERIFIED on this Powerwall. Not the public key.
data_description.cloud_backup: Also sign in to a Tesla account, so settings can still be changed through the Tesla cloud when the local connection is down.

wifi.title: Connect over the Powerwall's Wi-Fi
wifi.description: Home Assistant must be connected to the Powerwall's own Wi-Fi network (TeslaPW_…). This connection can read everything but cannot change settings or dispatch the battery; link a Tesla account to change settings through the cloud.

data.cloud_backup: Link a Tesla account to change settings

data_description.host: Usually `192.168.91.1`, the address of the Powerwall's own Wi-Fi network (TeslaPW_…).
data_description.cloud_backup: Without a Tesla account, this connection can only read. Sign in to change settings through the Tesla cloud.

login.title: Sign in to Tesla
login.description:
Your Tesla account is used to register the key with the Powerwall and as a backup for changing settings when the local connection is down.

**Browser sign-in:**
1. Open this link on a computer, with the browser's developer tools open on the **Network** tab (F12):
   [Sign in to Tesla]({url})
2. Sign in. The last page will not load, because Tesla sends the browser to a `tesla://auth/callback?code=…` address.
3. In the Network tab, find the request starting with `callback?code=` (or the `Location` header of the last redirect) and copy that full address.
4. Paste it below. Codes expire within minutes and work once.

**Or, a refresh token:** paste the refresh token from an app sign-in such as *Auth app for Tesla* (iOS, Android). Use a token made for this, not one another integration already uses: signing in elsewhere with the same token can log that integration out.

data_description.callback: The full `tesla://auth/callback?code=…` address from the browser sign-in, or a **refresh token** from an app sign-in (a long text, usually starting with `eyJ`). Each code works once and expires within minutes.

data_description.site: The energy site (Tesla app name) with this Powerwall. Choosing another site's Powerwall stops the setup.

verify_failed.title: The Powerwall did not confirm the key
verify_failed.description: No confirmation arrived in time (or the key was removed). Select **Submit** to register the key again and open a new 10-minute window, then do the switch step.

connect_failed.title: Could not connect
connect_failed.description: The last connection check failed (see the message below). Select **Submit** to go back and check the gateway address and password.

reauth_confirm.title: The Powerwall no longer accepts Home Assistant
reauth_confirm.description: The gateway keeps refusing the password or the key. Readings stop until this is fixed; settings still work through the Tesla cloud if an account is linked.

menu_options.register_fleet: Register the key again with my Tesla Fleet or Teslemetry integration

data_description.gw_pwd: The last 5 characters of the password on the QR sticker inside the Powerwall's cover (Powerwall 3: behind the front glass, lower left), or the whole password. Letters are upper case.

reconfigure.title: Change the connection
reconfigure.description: Give an RSA key file to use the signed (v1r) connection; leave it empty for the Wi-Fi password connection.

progress.confirm_key:
The key (fingerprint `{fingerprint}…`) is registered and waiting for physical confirmation. Within about 10 minutes:

- **Powerwall 3:** switch the On/Off switch (left side) OFF for about 15 seconds, then back ON. A short flick is ignored; leaving it off until the unit powers down closes the window.
- **Other models:** toggling the Powerwall's AC breaker off for about 15 seconds is reported to work on some units.

This page checks every 10 seconds and continues on its own once the Powerwall confirms. If the window closes, the key is registered again once automatically.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the Powerwall at that address. Check the address (your router lists the gateway as `teslapw_…`), that the Powerwall is on and on the same network as Home Assistant, and try again.
error.invalid_gw_pwd: The gateway refused this password. Check the QR sticker (letters are upper case).
error.password_required: Signed access needs the gateway password.
error.invalid_rsa_key: That is not an RSA private key in PEM format. Upload the private key file (it starts with `-----BEGIN`), not the public key.
error.key_not_accepted: The Powerwall did not accept the key. Check that it is the private key (not the public one), that it was registered for this Powerwall, and that the registration is VERIFIED (the On/Off switch step was done). Or choose **Register a new key**.
error.invalid_auth: Tesla did not accept that code. A new sign-in link has been made: sign in again with it and paste the new address, or paste a refresh token.
error.cloud_error: The Tesla service returned an error. Try again in a minute.
error.none_found: No Powerwall answered on this network. Enter the address instead (your router lists the gateway as `teslapw_…`).
error.owner_api_refused: You signed in, but the Tesla Owner API refused the token (HTTP 403). Sign in again; if it keeps happening, Tesla may have changed its sign-in rules again: please open an issue.
error.invalid_token: Tesla did not accept that refresh token. It may have expired or been used by another app: get a new one from your token app. The sign-in link has not changed.
error.invalid_callback: That is not a sign-in address from the link above. Paste the full `tesla://auth/callback?code=…` address from this link (an older link no longer works), or a refresh token. The link has not changed.

abort.already_configured: This Powerwall is already set up.
abort.no_sites: No Powerwall was found on this Tesla account. Sign in with the Tesla account that owns the Powerwall (the one that shows it in the Tesla app).
abort.register_failed: Tesla did not register the key. The likely causes: Tesla refused the sign-in token (sign in again with a fresh app sign-in), the wrong energy site was chosen, or Tesla can't reach the Powerwall right now (check it shows as online in the Tesla app). Start the setup again; the log has Tesla's exact answer.
abort.wrong_powerwall: That is a different Powerwall from the one being set up. Choose the energy site with this Powerwall, or check the gateway address.
abort.unique_id_mismatch: The gateway at that address is a different Powerwall. Enter this Powerwall's address, or add the other one as a new entry.
abort.register_token_refused: Tesla refused the sign-in token when registering the key. Start the setup again and sign in again (in the browser, or with a fresh refresh token).
abort.register_wrong_site: Tesla doesn't know that energy site on this account. Start the setup again and choose the site with this Powerwall, signed in with the Tesla account that owns it.
abort.register_unreachable: Tesla could not reach the Powerwall to register the key. Check that it shows as online in the Tesla app (its internet connection), wait a few minutes and start the setup again.
abort.register_fleet_unavailable: The Tesla Fleet or Teslemetry integration can no longer be used for this Powerwall: it isn't loaded, doesn't have this Powerwall, or its sign-in can't send commands (it needs the energy_cmds permission). Check that integration, or start the setup again and register with a Tesla sign-in.

data.restore_export: Restore settings when the Powerwall drops them
data.status_alert_events: Alert events for status alerts too
data.dispatch_floor_reserve: Discharges stop at the backup reserve

data_description.restore_export: The Powerwall sometimes loses its grid export rule and its grid charging setting from its own settings (seen hourly on a Powerwall 3); grid charging then turns on. When on, the setting you chose is written back within a minute or two (signed connection only).
data_description.status_alert_events: Status alerts such as "Export limited" describe normal operation and some come and go every few minutes; by default only notices, warnings and faults create Alert events.
data_description.problem_minutes: How long a warning or fault must last before the Problem sensor turns on and a repair is raised.
data_description.dispatch_floor_reserve: A discharge started without `min_soc` stops when the battery reaches the backup reserve.
data_description.dispatch_max_watts: Dispatch calls above this power are refused.

cloud_backup.title: Cloud backup
cloud_backup.description:
When the local connection can't read or change a setting, it goes through the Tesla cloud instead. Two backups can be used, alone or one after the other:

- **Owner API**: a Tesla account linked here (*Link a Tesla account*). Currently {owner}.
- **Tesla Fleet**: the sign-in of Home Assistant's Tesla Fleet or Teslemetry integration, which use Tesla's official Fleet API. A loaded entry with this Powerwall is currently {fleet}. Its site data is read without extra Tesla calls, and its token is never refreshed here, so it stays signed in.

With both, settings are read from the first one that answers, and a change goes to the first one that accepts it. Each backup is checked about once an hour; one that stops working gets its own repair while the other keeps going.

data_description.cloud_backends: Only the backups that are set up are offered. Changing a setting through Tesla Fleet counts as a command on that Tesla developer account (or Teslemetry subscription); reading costs nothing extra.

dispatch_battery_power.name: Dispatch battery power
dispatch_battery_power.description: Run the battery at a fixed power for a set time over the signed local connection. Positive watts discharge, negative watts charge, 0 holds the battery idle. Overrides the export setting; a discharge stops at the backup reserve unless `min_soc` is given (option). The integration renews the command every minute in short steps, so the Powerwall returns to normal within 5 minutes if Home Assistant stops. A new call replaces a running dispatch. Use at your own risk: dispatching the battery may affect your Powerwall warranty, which may cover unlimited cycles only for self-consumption, time-based control and backup.

min_soc.description: End a discharge when the battery level (Tesla app scale) falls to this percentage. Default: the backup reserve.

charge_to.description: Charge the battery at a set power over the signed local connection until it reaches the target level, or for at most the time limit. Charges from solar and, if grid charging is allowed, from the grid. Ends with event reason `target_reached` or `completed`. Use at your own risk: dispatching the battery may affect your Powerwall warranty, which may cover unlimited cycles only for self-consumption, time-based control and backup.

start_max_backup.description: Start a backup event over the signed local connection: the Powerwall charges to full (from the grid too) and keeps the battery full for the duration, as Storm Watch does. A new call replaces a running max backup.

go_off_grid.name: Go off-grid
go_off_grid.description: Disconnect the house from the grid over the signed local connection, like *Go off-grid* in the Tesla app. The house then runs on the battery and solar; solar stops for about 30 seconds while the grid contactor switches. The action waits up to 90 seconds until the gateway reports it off-grid. The integration reconnects at the end of the duration, or when the battery falls to the reconnect level, also after a restart.

config_entry_id.description: Only needed when more than one Powerwall is set up.

confirm.name: Confirm
confirm.description: Must be on: this switches the house off the grid.

duration_minutes.name: Duration
duration_minutes.description: Reconnect after this many minutes (up to 24 hours). Without it, the house stays off-grid until the battery reaches the reconnect level or you reconnect.

min_soc.name: Reconnect at
min_soc.description: Reconnect when the battery level (Tesla app scale) falls to this percentage. Default: the backup reserve.

reconnect_grid.name: Reconnect to the grid
reconnect_grid.description: Reconnect the house to the grid over the signed local connection, also after *Go off-grid* in the Tesla app. The action waits up to 90 seconds until the Powerwall starts syncing to the grid.

Short alerts like this are normal while the Powerwall restarts or after its On/Off switch is used; this one has lasted more than {minutes} minutes. Check the Tesla app. If it does not clear, contact your installer or Tesla. This notice disappears when the alert clears.

fleet_backup.title: Tesla Fleet cloud backup is not working
fleet_backup.description:
The Powerwall TEDAPI integration uses the Tesla Fleet (or Teslemetry) integration as a cloud backup for settings, and the last checks failed. Local readings and control are not affected.

Check that the Tesla Fleet or Teslemetry integration is enabled, loaded and signed in (re-authenticate it if it asks), and that this Powerwall is on its Tesla account. This notice disappears after the next successful check (about hourly). To stop using it, choose another cloud backup in this integration's options.

fleet_read_only.title: Tesla Fleet cloud backup can't change settings
fleet_read_only.description:
The Tesla Fleet (or Teslemetry) sign-in used as the cloud backup can read the Powerwall's settings but not change them: it lacks the **energy_cmds** (energy commands) scope. Settings changes fall back to the next cloud backup, if any.

Sign in to that integration again (re-configure or re-authenticate it) and allow the energy commands permission. This notice disappears at the next check after that.

off_grid_reconnect_failed.title: The Powerwall couldn't reconnect to the grid
off_grid_reconnect_failed.description: An off-grid run started by the Powerwall TEDAPI integration has ended, but reconnecting to the grid failed. The house still runs on the battery ({soc}%). The integration tries again every minute; if it keeps failing, reconnect in the Tesla app. This notice disappears once the Powerwall is back on the grid.

cloud_reserve_capped.title: Tesla's cloud capped the backup reserve
cloud_reserve_capped.description:
The backup reserve was set to {wanted}% through {backend}, but the Powerwall reports {actual}%. Tesla's cloud caps the reserve it sets at 80%.

To keep the battery fuller, use the **Start max backup** action (`tesla_tedapi.start_max_backup`), or set the reserve again while the signed local connection works: local writes are not capped.

cloud_write_mismatch.title: A cloud change did not apply as set
cloud_write_mismatch.description: A setting was changed to `{wanted}` through {backend}, but after 5 minutes the Powerwall reports `{actual}`. Tesla may have changed or refused it. Check the setting in the Tesla app, and set it again once the signed local connection works.

firmware_signed_access.title: Signed local access stopped after a firmware update
firmware_signed_access.description:
The Powerwall was updated from firmware {previous} to {version}, and it no longer answers the signed local connection. Tesla can change local access with an update.

Readings are unavailable; settings use the cloud backup if one is set up. This clears by itself when signed access works again. If it lasts, check for an update of this integration, or register the key again (**Configure → Register a new signed key**).
